newsitem.title: UK: IBCA ups Metway Bank to A from A minus.
newsitem.headline: IBCA ups Metway Bank to A from A minus.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said it has upgraded the long-term rating of Australia's Metway Bank Limited from A- (A minus) to A and removed it from RatingWatch with positive implications.

The bank's short-term rating was affirmed at A1. In addition, new Claims Settling Ability ratings were assigned to two insurance entities in the Metway group: an A+ (Good Security) to Suncorp General Insurance Ltd and an A- (A minus/Good Security) to Suncorp Life and Superannuation Ltd.
The ratings upgrade for Metway follows the amalgamation in December of four Queensland-based financiers and the two Suncorp insurers under the Metway umbrella.
The Queensland Government currently owns 67 percent of the enlarged group but intends to reduce this holding to 15 percent over the next five years.
As a result of the merger, Metway is now Australia's seventh largest banking group, with banking assets of around A$15 billion, IBCA said.

"The merger provides Metway with a range of benefits, including a more diversified loan portfolio; a significant share of the Queensland market; excellent group cross-selling opportunities; and potential economies of scale," IBCA said.

"Though the effect of the Government of Queensland guarantee will be removed following the merger, IBCA considers that the company will derive significant operational benefits from membership of the expanded group," IBCA said.
